items.title: Fermi America, Blue Energy make strides in Texas - American Nuclear Society -- ANS
items.excerpt: A draft environmental impact statement is now complete for Fermi America’s plan to construct and operate four AP1000 reactors at its Project Matador Advanced Energy and Intelligence Campus in Texas, a project that has seen upheaval along the way, including the ouster of cofounders from their leadership roles. Developed in partnership with Texas Tech University, Project Matador has been touted by Fermi America as one of the largest private energy grids of its kind. The plans originally called for a site with 11 GW of power, including 4.4 GW of nuclear generation, but more recent updates called for a campus that could generate closer to 17 GW of electricity.

items.summary: Toby R. Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., has suspended his current proxy campaign to call a special meeting of shareholders due to a judge's last-minute recusal, which has disrupted the timeline for the strategic process. Despite having earned the backing of leading proxy advisory firms and a majority of votes cast, Neugebauer will continue to push for good governance through the judicial process. Neugebauer remains confident in Fermi's ability to secure a tenant group and achieve long-term success, and has pledged to monitor the board's execution and resume his campaign if necessary to safeguard the value of Project Matador.

items.summary: Toby R. Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., disclosed that the company has dropped its lawsuit against him, which was filed to validate a 70% supermajority bylaw amendment, after a Texas Business Court ordered the company to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players. The move is seen as a significant development in the ongoing governance dispute at Fermi, with Neugebauer arguing that the board's actions were an attempt to entrench itself and avoid scrutiny.

items.title: Can Trump Fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook?
items.summary: For more than a year, President Donald Trump has sought to push out members of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors and gain more leverage over the central bank’s policies. In early October, the White House resumed that effort, announcing the formation of a committee to investigate mortgage fraud allegations against board member Lisa Cook. She will be required to appear at a White House hearing on Nov. 5 to defend herself, Trump said in a memo.

It's called surveillance pricing and retailers like Walmart appear to be locking down technology that will help them figure out how much they can charge you. items.title: Oracle Trucking Gas to Keep Data Centers on Track
items.summary: Oracle is using a new power strategy to keep many of its data centers on track: trucking natural gas directly to the server farms. The company is considering using this approach to speed up a build in New Mexico, where a gas pipeline needed to help power one of its crucial data centers is delayed. Bloomberg's Brody Ford joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech" to discuss Oracle's strategy. (Source: Bloomberg)
